description: This topic explores drama as a literary genre, covering its types, elements, dramatic techniques, themes, and the roles involved in turning a written play into a live performance.

mcq.questionText: What is drama as a form of literature?

options.text: A story told only through descriptive paragraphs
A literary work written to be performed on stage by actors
A collection of rhyming lines arranged in stanzas
A factual account of real historical events

mcq.explanation: Drama is a literary genre written mainly to be acted out on a stage by performers before an audience.

mcq.questionText: How does drama mainly differ from prose?

options.text: Drama uses dialogue and action to tell the story, while prose uses narrative description
Drama always rhymes while prose never does
Drama cannot have characters but prose must have them
Prose is meant to be performed but drama is meant to be read silently

mcq.explanation: Drama unfolds chiefly through the dialogue and actions of characters, whereas prose relies on a narrator's description and narration.

mcq.questionText: A play that ends in disaster, suffering or the downfall of the main character is called a:
mcq.explanation: A tragedy is a serious play that ends unhappily, usually with the suffering or downfall of the protagonist.

mcq.questionText: Which type of drama is light, amusing and usually ends happily?
mcq.explanation: A comedy is a humorous play designed to amuse the audience and normally has a happy ending.

mcq.questionText: A play that mixes both serious (tragic) and humorous (comic) elements is called a:
mcq.explanation: Tragicomedy blends tragic and comic features in one play, so the mood shifts between serious and light.

mcq.questionText: A farce is best described as a type of drama that:

options.text: Relies on exaggerated, ridiculous situations to create laughter
Always ends with the hero's death
Contains only sad and serious events

mcq.explanation: A farce is a low form of comedy that uses absurd, exaggerated and improbable situations to make the audience laugh.

mcq.questionText: In drama, the major divisions of a play are called acts, and the smaller divisions within an act are called:
mcq.explanation: A play is divided into acts, and each act is further broken into smaller units called scenes.

mcq.questionText: A long speech delivered by a character who is alone on stage, revealing his or her private thoughts, is a:
mcq.explanation: A soliloquy is a speech a character makes while alone, sharing inner thoughts and feelings with the audience.

mcq.questionText: When a character makes a short remark to the audience that other characters on stage are not supposed to hear, this is called a/an:
mcq.explanation: An aside is a brief comment spoken directly to the audience and not heard by the other characters.

mcq.questionText: The conversation between two or more characters in a play is known as:
mcq.explanation: Dialogue is the spoken exchange between characters and is the main way a story is told in drama.

mcq.questionText: Instructions written in a play to tell actors how to move, speak or behave on stage are called:
mcq.explanation: Stage directions are the playwright's notes (often in brackets or italics) guiding actors' actions, movements and tone.

mcq.questionText: In a play, the point of highest tension where the conflict reaches its peak is the:
mcq.explanation: The climax is the moment of greatest tension or turning point in the plot, where conflict reaches its highest point.

mcq.questionText: A situation in which the audience knows something important that a character on stage does not know is called:
mcq.explanation: Dramatic irony occurs when the audience possesses knowledge that a character lacks, creating tension or humour.

mcq.questionText: Who is the person that writes a play?
mcq.explanation: A playwright is the author who writes the script of a play (a dramatist).

mcq.questionText: The central idea or underlying message that a play communicates to its audience is called the:
mcq.explanation: The theme is the main idea, lesson or message that a literary work, including a play, conveys.

fib.questionText: A literary work written mainly to be performed on stage by actors is called _____.
fib.explanation: Drama is the genre meant for performance on stage before an audience.

fib.questionText: A serious play that ends in the suffering or downfall of the main character is a _____.
fib.explanation: A tragedy is a serious play with an unhappy ending, usually the protagonist's downfall.

fib.questionText: A humorous play that amuses the audience and usually ends happily is a _____.
fib.explanation: A comedy is light and amusing and typically ends well.

fib.questionText: A speech delivered by a character who is alone on stage, revealing inner thoughts, is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A soliloquy lets the audience hear a lone character's private thoughts.

fib.questionText: The conversation between two or more characters in a play is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Dialogue is the spoken exchange between characters and drives the play forward.

fib.questionText: The struggle between opposing forces or characters in a play is called _____.
fib.explanation: Conflict is the central struggle that creates tension and drives the plot of a play.

fib.questionText: Bracketed instructions telling actors how to move and speak on stage are called stage _____.
fib.explanation: Stage directions guide the actors' movements, gestures and delivery.

fib.questionText: The time and place in which the events of a play happen are called the _____.
fib.explanation: The setting is the time and location where the action of a play takes place.

fib.questionText: A technique that interrupts the present action to show events that happened earlier is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A flashback takes the story back in time to reveal earlier events.

fib.questionText: The person who guides actors and oversees the production of a play on stage is the _____.
fib.explanation: The director interprets the script and guides actors and the whole production.

tf.questionText: Drama is written mainly to be performed on stage rather than only to be read silently.
tf.explanation: The primary purpose of drama is performance before an audience, although it can also be read.

tf.questionText: In drama the story is told mainly through the dialogue and actions of characters rather than through a narrator's description.
tf.explanation: Unlike prose, drama relies on dialogue and action instead of a narrator.

tf.questionText: A comedy normally ends with the death or downfall of its main character.
tf.explanation: A comedy is amusing and usually ends happily; it is tragedy that ends in downfall.

tf.questionText: A soliloquy is a conversation between two or more characters.
tf.explanation: A soliloquy is spoken by a character who is alone; a conversation between characters is dialogue.

tf.questionText: An aside is a remark made by a character that the audience hears but the other characters are not supposed to hear.
tf.explanation: An aside is directed to the audience and assumed unheard by other characters on stage.

tf.questionText: A play is divided into acts, and each act may be divided into scenes.
tf.explanation: Acts are the major divisions of a play and scenes are the smaller units within an act.

tf.questionText: Dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows something that a character on stage does not know.
tf.explanation: Dramatic irony arises from the gap between what the audience knows and what a character knows.

tf.questionText: A tragicomedy contains only serious events and no humour at all.
tf.explanation: A tragicomedy mixes both tragic (serious) and comic (humorous) elements.

tf.questionText: The climax of a play is the point where the conflict reaches its highest tension.
tf.explanation: The climax is the peak or turning point of the plot where tension is greatest.

tf.questionText: The playwright and the director are always the same person in every theatre production.
tf.explanation: The playwright writes the script while the director stages it; they are usually different people.

summary.questionText: In two or three sentences, explain what drama is and state its main purpose.
summary.correctAnswer: Drama is a genre of literature written in the form of dialogue and action and meant to be performed on stage by actors. Its main purpose is to present a story to a live audience through performance, while also entertaining and teaching.
summary.explanation: A good answer defines drama as a performance-based genre using dialogue and action, and notes its purpose to entertain, educate and present a story to an audience.

summary.questionText: Briefly explain two main differences between drama and prose.
summary.correctAnswer: First, drama tells its story mainly through dialogue and the actions of characters, while prose tells it through a narrator's description and narration. Second, drama is written to be performed on stage, while prose is written mainly to be read.
summary.explanation: Accept any two valid contrasts: use of dialogue/action versus narration, performance versus reading, division into acts/scenes versus chapters/paragraphs.

summary.questionText: Name and briefly describe the four main types of drama.
summary.correctAnswer: Tragedy is a serious play ending in suffering or the downfall of the hero. Comedy is a light, amusing play that usually ends happily. Tragicomedy mixes both tragic and comic elements. Farce is an exaggerated, ridiculous form of comedy meant to provoke laughter.
summary.explanation: The answer should list tragedy, comedy, tragicomedy and farce with a short, accurate description of each.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between a soliloquy, a monologue and an aside.
summary.correctAnswer: A soliloquy is a speech by a character who is alone on stage, revealing private thoughts. A monologue is a long speech by one character, which may be addressed to other characters or the audience. An aside is a short remark spoken to the audience that the other characters are not supposed to hear.
summary.explanation: Accept answers showing soliloquy = alone, revealing inner thoughts; monologue = long single speech (may have listeners); aside = brief remark to audience unheard by others.

summary.questionText: Explain what is meant by the plot of a play.
summary.correctAnswer: The plot is the arrangement or sequence of events in a play, showing how one event leads to another from the beginning, through the rising action and climax, to the resolution. It is the storyline that holds the actions of the characters together.
summary.explanation: A correct answer defines plot as the ordered sequence of events/storyline, ideally mentioning its stages.

summary.questionText: What is conflict in a play, and why is it important?
summary.correctAnswer: Conflict is the struggle between opposing forces, such as between two characters, or between a character and society, nature or his or her own feelings. It is important because it creates tension and interest and drives the plot of the play forward.
summary.explanation: The answer should define conflict as a struggle between opposing forces and note that it generates tension and moves the plot.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between dramatic irony and suspense.
summary.correctAnswer: Dramatic irony is when the audience knows something important that a character on stage does not know. Suspense is the feeling of anxiety or excitement created when the audience is uncertain about what will happen next.
summary.explanation: Dramatic irony = gap in knowledge between audience and character; suspense = uncertainty/tension about future events.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between a play as a written text and a play as a performance.
summary.correctAnswer: As a written text, a play is a script made up of dialogue and stage directions that can be read on paper. As a performance, the same play is brought to life on stage by actors, with movement, voice, costume, lighting and an audience watching. The text is the plan, while the performance is its living realisation.
summary.explanation: Accept answers contrasting the script (read on paper) with the live staged production (acted out with actors, set, audience).

summary.questionText: State the main roles of the playwright, the director and the actors in theatre.
summary.correctAnswer: The playwright writes the script of the play. The director interprets the script and guides the actors and the whole production. The actors perform the characters on stage before the audience.
summary.explanation: The answer should match each role correctly: playwright writes, director guides/interprets, actors perform.

summary.questionText: What is the theme of a play, and how does it differ from the plot?
summary.correctAnswer: The theme is the central idea or message the play communicates, such as love, betrayal or corruption. The plot is the actual sequence of events that takes place. The plot is what happens, while the theme is the underlying meaning or lesson behind what happens.
summary.explanation: Theme = central idea/message; plot = sequence of events. The answer should clearly separate meaning from events.

hoq.questionText:
Read the short extract and answer the question.

MAUA: (smiling warmly) I am so glad you came, Juma. You are the most honest trader in this whole market.
JUMA: (turning to the audience, lowering his voice) If only she knew the sack of maize I sold her last week was half stones.
MAUA: Did you say something?
JUMA: Nothing, my friend. Nothing at all.

The words Juma speaks while turning to the audience are an example of which dramatic device?

options.text: A soliloquy, because Juma is alone on stage
An aside, because he speaks to the audience and Maua is not meant to hear it
A stage direction, because it tells him how to move
A flashback, because it returns to an earlier event

hoq.explanation: Juma is on stage with Maua but turns to the audience with a remark she is not supposed to hear, which is the definition of an aside. It is not a soliloquy because he is not alone.

hoq.questionText:
Read the short extract and answer the question.

NURSE: (cheerfully arranging flowers) The doctor says you will be well in time for your wedding next month, dear Halima.
HALIMA: (weakly) I cannot wait to walk down the aisle.
(The audience has just heard the doctor tell the family, in an earlier scene, that Halima has only days to live.)

What dramatic technique is most clearly being used in this extract?

options.text: Suspense, because no one knows what will happen
Comic relief, because the scene is funny
Dramatic irony, because the audience knows Halima is dying while she hopes for her wedding
A monologue, because one character speaks at length

hoq.explanation: The audience already knows the truth about Halima's condition that she and the nurse seem hopeful about, creating a painful gap in knowledge, which is dramatic irony.

hoq.questionText:
Read the short extract and answer the question.

(Late at night. KAREMA stands alone in the empty courtroom, holding the stolen verdict papers.)
KAREMA: They call me a man of justice, yet here I am, ready to bury the truth for a handful of money. What kind of judge have I become? My father would weep to see me now.

The speech made by Karema in this extract is best described as a:

options.text: Dialogue, because he is talking with another character
Soliloquy, because he is alone and reveals his inner thoughts and conscience
Aside, because it is a very short remark to the audience
Stage direction, because it appears in brackets

hoq.explanation: Karema is alone on stage and openly reveals his private thoughts and troubled conscience, which is the defining feature of a soliloquy.
